results.title: General Manager – Logistics Stockyard (Automotive)
results.description: The Job Summary The General Manager leads Petromin Logistics' stockyard as a profitable, customer-focused and technology-driven automotive logistics business. The role owns the full P&L, acquires and retains vehicle-brand accounts, and delivers reliable service across the vehicle lifecycle, driving the stockyard's launch and growth through digital operations, financial discipline and continuous improvement. Key Performance Indicators / Measures: • Revenue, operating profit and cash flow vs. the approved business plan • Customer margin, cost per vehicle and capacity utilisation • New vehicle-brand accounts won and growth of existing accounts • Customer satisfaction, retention and SLA achievement • Vehicle turnaround, dispatch reliability and PDI first-time-right • Damage, rework and claims recovery • Digital and AI use cases delivered, with measured gains in productivity, accuracy and cost • Safety, quality and business-continuity performance; team capability The KPIs listed in this JD define what the role is measured on; specific targets and weights are set and may be adjusted annually through the performance management cycle, in agreement with the line manager. Technical / Job-Specific Competencies 1 Business Plan & P&L Ownership Own the stockyard business plan, budget and P&L, and drive pricing, cost control, billing and collections, to deliver revenue, profit and cash targets. 2 Profitability & Investment Manage profitability by customer and service, cost per vehicle and break-even utilisation, and build investment cases for capacity and technology, to secure measurable returns. 3 Strategic Account Acquisition Personally lead account acquisition with Business Development, winning OEM, vehicle-brand, importer and distributor business through strong relationships and competitive proposals, to grow and diversify revenue. 4 Contracts & Account Growth Negotiate contracts and service levels with Finance and Legal, and grow existing accounts in line with operational capacity, to secure profitable, sustainable business. 5 Digital Strategy & Systems Lead the stockyard's digital strategy, integrating YMS, ERP, transport and customer systems, to give real-time vehicle visibility, accurate inventory and digital workflows. 6 AI & Automation Adoption Prioritise and implement AI and automation for capacity planning, vehicle allocation, damage detection, predictive maintenance and reporting, with Corporate IT ensuring data quality, security and responsible AI use, to lower cost and raise productivity. 7 Stockyard Launch & Operations Lead readiness, launch and daily operations across receipt, storage, stock preservation, PDI, VAS, customs coordination and dispatch, and control outsourced service performance, to run a reliable, efficient stockyard. 8 Customer Experience & SLAs Deliver customer SLAs, resolve escalations and improve turnaround, productivity and vehicle condition through standard procedures and root-cause problem-solving, to raise satisfaction and retention. 9 People Leadership Develop accountable managers and digitally capable teams, and align workforce capacity and shared-service levels with business needs, to deliver the business plan. 10 Safety, Quality & Governance Own safety, quality, vehicle custody and business continuity, oversee damage prevention and claims recovery, and strengthen the Integrated Management System, reporting performance and risks to the CEO, to protect people, vehicles and the business. The Job Profile 1 Educational Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration or a related discipline. An MBA or relevant postgraduate qualification is preferred. 2 Professional Certifications No mandatory certification. A logistics or supply chain certification (e.g., ASCM CLTD / CSCP, CILT) is an advantage. 3 Experience 15+ years of relevant experience, including 5 years in senior leadership with direct P&L accountability; Saudi or GCC experience is preferred. 4 Essential Job Pre-Requisites Strong finished-vehicle logistics experience (stockyard operations, PDI, transportation, outsourced services), including launching or substantially improving a stockyard or comparable operation. Proven personal success winning and retaining OEM, importer, distributor or major logistics accounts. Demonstrated delivery of YMS, WMS, TMS or ERP integration or comparable digital transformation, with measurable results. 5 Languages Proficiency Fluency in English and Arabic is mandatory.

results.title: Distribution Manager
results.description: Job description: Job Purpose: The Distribution Manager is responsible for leading and optimizing last mile delivery operations, ensuring the timely, efficient and cost-effective delivery of Marketplace and Xcite C&C products to customers. The role is accountable for managing delivery and administrative teams; driving operational excellence; improving customer experience and Net Promoter Scores (NPS); implementing technology-driven solutions; and achieving key operational, financial and service performance targets. Duties & Essential: Lead, coach & develop delivery teams and administrative staff to achieve operational excellence and high performance Manage last mile delivery operations, including scheduling, routing, dispatching & resource planning Establish, monitor and drive KPIs related to productivity, service quality, operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. Coordinate with warehouses, showrooms, customer service teams and business stakeholders to ensure seamless order fulfillment and delivery execution. Ensure delivery accuracy, service reliability and on-time performance to deliver an exceptional customer experience. Monitor NPS and customer feedback, resolve escalations promptly and implement initiatives to improve customer satisfaction. Oversee fleet operations, vehicle maintenance, and transportation resources while ensuring compliance with safety and regulatory standards. Drive process improvements, automation initiatives, and technology solutions to enhance operational efficiency, productivity, and cost optimization. Develop, implement, and continuously improve SOPs, operational controls and Health & Safety best practices across delivery operations. Utilize data analytics and performance reporting to identify trends, support decision-making, and drive continuous improvement and operational excellence. Skills/Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in relevant field Proven experience in logistics, supply chain management or a related field, with a focus on last mile delivery. Strong leadership and team management skills. Excellent organizational and problem-solving abilities. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

results.title: Sr. Manager Logistics Operations
results.description: Talabat is part of the Delivery Hero Group, the world’s pioneering local delivery platform, our mission is to deliver an amazing experience—fast, easy, and to your door. We operate in around 65 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Delivery Hero has been listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange since 2017 and is part of the MDAX stock market index. Job Description WHAT’S ON YOUR PLATE? Lead Talabat Qatar’s overall supply ecosystem, ensuring a sustainable, high-quality, and high-performing rider base across the country. Develop and execute the overall supply growth and acquisition strategy aligned with business demand and market dynamics. Lead long-term supply forecasting and planning to ensure full coverage and service level adherence. Identify and launch new supply channels such as female riders, refugees, micro-financing, and e-bikes to diversify and sustain fleet growth. Manage the full lifecycle of 3PL partnerships, from selection and onboarding to performance management and contract renewals. Set clear KPIs and SLAs for 3PL partners, ensuring compliance, efficiency, and rider quality. Build and maintain strong strategic relationships with key 3PL partners to drive alignment and operational excellence. Lead and manage the on-ground operations team to ensure smooth daily operations, compliance, and service quality. Monitor and improve key operational KPIs including rider supply rate, EPH, order-on-time percentage, and churn rate. Implement standardized processes and digital tools to enhance control, visibility, and scalability across operations. Coach and develop a high-performing team of managers, seniors, and specialists across supply, 3PLs, and operations. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement within the team. Work closely with cross-functional teams such as People, Finance, Commercial, and Product to align on strategies and deliverables. Identify and implement process improvements and best practices to enhance efficiency and rider satisfaction. Drive automation and technology-enabled initiatives to improve visibility and performance management. Oversee equipment management including uniforms, delivery boxes, and e-bikes to ensure consistent quality and operational standards. Ensure adherence to performance KPIs such as supply run rate, rider churn and retention, 3PL compliance, rider NPS, EPH, and operational coverage. Build long-term plans to sustain growth and strengthen Talabat’s market leadership position. Qualifications WHAT DID WE ORDER? Bachelor’s degree required, with a preference for majors in Logistics, Supply Chain, Operations, or equivalent work experience in compliance or auditing Minimum of 5 years of experience in operational roles within fast-paced environments. Track record in the FoodTech logistics sector is a plus. Management consulting experience is also considered a significant advantage Management experience is advantageous, with the ability to effectively manage direct reports and foster a strong team culture. Strong problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to dig into detail, manage complexity, and drive decision-making Advanced proficiency in GSheet, demonstrating a strong analytical skill set. Ability to reason analytically, logically, and in a consistent fashion Strong English written and verbal communication skills, capable of engaging across a diverse set of stakeholders, Arabic is good to have but not necessary Extremely organized and process-driven, with a proven ability to manage a heavy workload effectively by setting priorities and managing expectations well Able to travel to all talabat markets as needed.

results.title: Managing Director - Contract Logistics
results.description: Managing Director - Contract Logistics (Riyadh, Saudi Arabia) About the Opportunity A leading global supply chain and logistics organisation is undertaking a major expansion across the Middle East and Africa as part of its long-term growth strategy. With Saudi Arabia identified as a key growth engine for the region, the business is making significant investments to build and scale its operations across the Kingdom. As part of this investment, the business is launching and scaling a strategic joint venture focused on large-scale logistics, transportation, warehousing and supply chain operations across Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East. The organisation is seeking an experienced Managing Director to build, lead and grow this business from the ground up. The Role The Managing Director will take full responsibility for the growth, operational performance and strategic development of a newly established supply chain and logistics platform in Saudi Arabia. This is a rare opportunity to lead a high-profile growth venture backed by a global market leader, with responsibility for scaling operations, developing commercial partnerships, building high-performing teams and delivering significant revenue growth. The successful candidate will operate at both strategic and operational levels, driving market expansion while ensuring world-class service delivery and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Lead the overall strategy and execution of a high-growth contract logistics and transportation business. Build and scale operations across KSA. Develop and execute commercial growth plans to achieve ambitious revenue and profitability targets. Establish and lead high-performing operational, commercial and functional teams. Manage significant P&L responsibility and drive financial performance. Build strong relationships with customers, strategic partners, government entities and key stakeholders. Identify and capitalise on opportunities for operational expansion and market growth. Drive organisational transformation in a fast-growth environment. Implement best-in-class safety, operational and customer service standards. Work collaboratively within a joint venture structure, aligning multiple stakeholder interests while delivering commercial outcomes. Candidate Profile Essential Experience Proven experience leading a sizeable contract logistics, supply chain or integrated logistics business. Track record of scaling operations and delivering accelerated growth. Strong strategic and commercial leadership capability. Experience managing large operational teams and complex customer portfolios. Demonstrated success managing a €300M+ P&L and delivering sustainable revenue and profitability growth. Background within contract logistics, supply chain management, transportation or distribution. Experience operating in Saudi Arabia and/or the wider Middle East. Preferred Experience Experience launching, integrating or scaling new business ventures. Exposure to joint venture, partnership or multi-stakeholder operating models. Experience within industrial, energy, infrastructure, FMCG, agriculture or large-scale logistics environments. Strong understanding of transportation networks, distribution operations and supply chain solutions. Leadership Competencies The successful candidate will demonstrate: Strong customer orientation and commercial acumen. Inspirational and people-focused leadership style. Ability to build and develop high-performing teams. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills. High levels of emotional intelligence and cultural awareness. Resilience and adaptability within a rapidly evolving business environment. Strong execution capability with a hands-on leadership approach. Location Riyadh, Saudi Arabia The role requires a strong on-the-ground presence and will play a key role in shaping the organisation's long-term growth strategy across the Kingdom. Why Join? Opportunity to lead one of the most significant logistics growth initiatives in the Middle East. Full ownership of a high-profile business scaling journey. Backing of a globally recognised supply chain organisation. Significant autonomy and visibility with senior regional leadership. Long-term career progression within a rapidly growing regional business.

results.title: Regional Logistics Manager - Middle East
results.description: About The Job The Logistics Manager runs the flow of goods between Origins, the Dubai distribution Centre and 24 stores in six countries, from inbound to store delivery, through customs and regulatory compliance. This role manages four Logistics Executives, owns the carrier and broker relationships, and is accountable for service, cost and compliance on every lane. The role turns a team of strong individual owners into one operation: shared priorities, one escalation path, one set of KPIs read by supply chain, retail, merchandising and finance. Job responsibilities Team leadership Lead, develop and evaluate the four Logistics Executives; set objectives, run the weekly logistics review, hold the mid-year and annual reviews. Keep ownership clear: one owner and one backup per task, cover during leave and peaks. Be the single escalation point for stores, merchandising and retail on any logistics topic. Inbound and control tower Own end-to-end visibility from departure in Europe to store receipt: in-transit tracking, lead times, claims. Steer the inbound forwarder: capacity planning, service levels, rate card application, invoice reconciliation. Plan and secure the inbound for events, window installations and store openings. Customs, duties and regulatory Guarantee customs compliance in six countries: declarations, duty optimization, audits, archives. Own product regulatory affairs with the local authorities and inspection bodies: registrations, licenses, CITES. Keep business continuity plans current for regulated categories. Carriers, brokers and tenders Manage the carrier and broker portfolio: contracts, SLAs, performance reviews, claims and insurance. Lead tenders and renewals with Legal and the central transport team. Drive carrier integrations with the delivery management platform so every shipment is tracked end to end. Cost and performance Own the logistics budget lines: transport, customs, brokerage and packaging. Validate the full cost monthly; challenge every deviation from the agreed rate cards. Publish the logistics KPIs to retail, merchandising and finance: lead time, on-time delivery, cost per unit, claims, compliance. Operations and projects Prepare network changes with the distribution center. Document and improve the SOPs. Profile Experience 6 to 10 years in logistics or supply chain, with at least 3 years managing a team. Hands-on knowledge of GCC customs and regulatory frameworks. Track record with freight forwarders, express carriers and customs brokers: contracts, SLAs, disputes. Luxury, fashion or high-value goods logistics is a strong plus; events logistics an advantage. Skills SAP, Excel at advanced level, Power BI for reporting. Cost control: rate cards, invoice reconciliation, budget follow-up. Contract & Tender Management in Transportation & Customs Brokerage services Structured writing and presenting, in English, for retail and executive audiences. Behaviors Calm under peak pressure and able to decide fast with partial information. Develops people: gives ownership, coaches, holds the line on standards. Rigorous on compliance; comfortable saying no to a store or a supplier when the rule requires it. Languages English fluent. French and/or Arabic an asset. Reference LVM34224

results.title: Senior Logistics, Security and Interface Manager
results.description: Position Overview We are seeking an experienced Senior Logistics, Security & Interface Manager to oversee and coordinate logistics operations, site security, and interface management across large-scale construction and engineering projects. The successful candidate will have extensive hands-on site experience, preferably within major infrastructure, mixed-use, industrial, or other complex development projects. The role requires strong leadership and coordination capabilities to ensure the efficient movement of resources, materials, equipment, and personnel, while maintaining robust site security arrangements and effective coordination among contractors, consultants, project stakeholders, and relevant authorities. Key Responsibilities Logistics Management Develop, implement, and oversee comprehensive site logistics plans for large-scale construction and engineering projects Manage site access, traffic management, transportation routes, material deliveries, storage, laydown areas, and heavy equipment movements Coordinate logistics requirements with construction teams, subcontractors, suppliers, and project management consultants Ensure efficient utilization of site resources and minimize logistical constraints that may impact construction progress Identify potential logistical risks and implement mitigation measures to maintain uninterrupted site operations Monitor logistics performance and ensure compliance with project requirements, applicable regulations, and safety standards Security Management Develop and implement project-wide security strategies, policies, and procedures to safeguard personnel, assets, equipment, and project facilities Oversee site security operations, including access control, perimeter security, surveillance, visitor management, and security personnel Coordinate with security contractors, local authorities, emergency response teams, and other relevant stakeholders Conduct security risk assessments and implement appropriate preventive and contingency measures Investigate security incidents and ensure timely reporting, documentation, and corrective actions Ensure security arrangements are aligned with project requirements and applicable local regulations Interface Management Lead and coordinate interfaces between construction contractors, engineering consultants, project management teams, utility providers, government entities, and other stakeholders Identify, monitor, and resolve physical, operational, logistical, and organizational interface issues across project packages Establish effective interface coordination procedures, communication protocols, and reporting mechanisms Facilitate interface meetings and ensure timely resolution of issues affecting construction activities and project delivery Maintain interface registers, action trackers, risk logs, and coordination plans Proactively identify potential conflicts between contractors, construction activities, and project infrastructure to avoid delays and disruptions Leadership & Reporting Provide strategic direction and leadership to logistics, security, and interface teams Monitor departmental performance against project schedules, milestones, and operational objectives Prepare management reports, performance dashboards, risk assessments, and progress updates Work closely with the Project Director, Construction Director, and other senior project stakeholders to ensure seamless project execution Drive continuous improvement in logistics efficiency, security management, and interface coordination Requirements Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Logistics, Security Management, or a related discipline Minimum 15 years of relevant professional experience, with substantial exposure to large-scale construction, engineering, infrastructure, or mega development projects Extensive hands-on experience in site-based logistics management, security operations, and construction interface coordination Proven experience managing complex construction sites involving multiple contractors, work packages, and project stakeholders Strong understanding of construction logistics, traffic management, site access control, security protocols, and interface management processes Experience working within a PMC, EPC, main contractor, or major project delivery environment is preferred Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and coordinate with senior project management and external stakeholders Excellent communication, negotiation, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills Strong reporting, planning, risk management, and organizational capabilities Preferred Experience Experience working on major GCC construction, infrastructure, or giga-project developments Exposure to complex, multi-package construction environments with significant logistical and security requirements Familiarity with local authority requirements, security regulations, and construction site operational standards in the GCC Professional certifications in logistics, security management, project management, or interface management would be an advantage

results.title: Director of Operations
results.location: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
results.description: Job Description Company Description Emirates Electrical & Instrumentation Company LLC. For almost 20 years, we have made vital contributions to the Oil & Gas sector of the UAE, executing both onshore and offshore projects. Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) is one of our main clients along with Tier 1 and Tier 2 EPC contractors in this sector. We have the expertise to carry out full EPC&M services for electrical and instrumentation works and bring our intrinsic knowledge to measure and automate exploration, production, separation, refining processes, and distribution through our localized services. Job Summary Reporting to the General Manager, the Director of Operations leads the operational and financial performance of EEIC's EPC projects and service divisions (Maintenance Contracts and Secondment Services), owning the Operations P&L, budgets, forecasts, OPEX, gross profit, cash flow and resources, and ensuring delivery to contract, schedule, HSE, quality and profit targets. The role protects and improves margins through robust budgeting, monitoring, corrective action, cost optimisation and variation recovery, ensuring forecasts are backed by validated progress, realistic cost-to-complete and quantified risks. It resolves issues within delegated authority and escalates material matters to the General Manager with impact and recommendations. Leading the Head of Projects, Engineering Manager and Head of Division, and through them Project Managers and teams, the role strengthens leadership, governance and execution standards. It requires a commercially astute EPC professional with contractor-side experience managing multiple projects across planning, engineering, procurement, construction, subcontracting and clients Duties & Responsibilities Financial, Budget & P&L Management Own the financial performance and P&L of the Operations Department, including the EPC project portfolio and operational service divisions, ensuring achievement of approved revenue, gross profit and profitability targets, and provide the General Manager with timely visibility of material financial deviations, risks and opportunities. Lead preparation of the annual Operations Department budget (revenue, gross profit, OPEX, manpower and other cost assumptions), provide reliable operational inputs to the General Manager and Finance for business planning, and control OPEX within approved budgets. Lead and challenge individual project budgets following award, ensuring they reflect the approved commercial baseline, execution strategy, resources, procurement and subcontracting strategy, risks and expected profitability, and endorse budgets and revisions in accordance with the Delegation of Authority. Review project P&Ls regularly – revenue, actual and committed costs, accruals, cost-to-complete, EAC, gross profit, margin and cash flow – and hold Head of Projects and Project Managers accountable for budget ownership and financial performance. Ensure accurate monthly, quarterly and annual forecasts of revenue, cost, GP and cash flow, supported by validated progress, realistic cost-to-complete, contractual entitlements, committed costs and quantified risks and opportunities. Identify margin erosion and cost overruns early, establish root causes and drive corrective action, and lead initiatives to protect and improve gross profit – through cost optimisation, productivity, procurement savings, variation recovery and improved execution methods – without compromising HSE, quality, contractual or client requirements. Monitor billing, certification, unbilled revenue, receivables and cash collection in coordination with Commercial and Finance, ensuring alignment with physical progress and revenue recognition. Ensure operational managers own and validate their financial assumptions, delivery commitments and recovery plans. Finance supports reporting and validation; the Director of Operations remains accountable for operational forecasts and performance commitments. Project Delivery & Operational Management Lead and oversee the execution of EEIC's EPC project portfolio from award through engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning and close-out, in accordance with contractual requirements, approved budgets, baseline schedules, HSE and quality standards. Oversee the Maintenance Contracts and Secondment Services divisions, ensuring service levels, manpower utilisation, contract renewals and divisional profitability meet approved targets. Ensure appropriate execution strategies, mobilization plans and project management structures are established for newly awarded projects. Conduct structured project performance reviews covering progress, schedule, cost, profitability, cash flow, engineering, procurement, construction, subcontracting, resources, commercial matters and key risks, maintaining portfolio-level visibility of status, milestones and priorities. Identify underperforming projects early and lead the development and implementation of corrective action and recovery plans. Ensure effective coordination between Projects, Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Planning & Project Controls, Commercial, Finance, HSE and Quality functions. Optimize manpower, equipment and other resources across the project portfolio according to operational priorities. Provide visible HSE leadership across all projects and service sites, ensuring HSE plans, resources and performance meet company and client (including ADNOC) requirements. Provide timely, accurate reporting to the General Manager and escalate material operational, financial, contractual and client risks with quantified impact, actions taken and clear recommendations, after review and challenge through the management hierarchy. Take ownership of resolving operational matters within delegated authority, ensuring that the Head of Projects, Head of Division and Project Managers remain accountable for their respective responsibilities. Escalate matters requiring executive intervention in a timely manner, without unnecessarily transferring routine operational management responsibilities to the General Manager. Planning, Project Controls & EPC Oversight Oversee, through the Head of Project Controls and Head of Projects, the planning and project controls framework, ensuring baseline programmes, progress measurement and reporting are consistently applied across all projects. Review portfolio-level schedule performance, critical-path risks and key milestones through regular operational reviews, challenging delays, unrealistic forecasts and deviations from approved plans. Review, endorse and drive the implementation of recovery and acceleration strategies for projects at risk, ensuring that required resources, cost implications, contractual considerations and management support are adequately assessed, with approvals obtained in accordance with the company's Delegation of Authority. Ensure effective integration of engineering, procurement and construction across the port
